text:
maya: Customer ticket says Python stream generator hangs sporadically when auth is rotated mid-stream. They see a few 401s, then the SSE generator never yields again. attaching brief logs and repro steps.

samir: can you paste the minimal repro steps + sdk version and whether they're using header token or cookie refresh?

maya: steps: 1) start long-running streaming call to /v1/streams with python sdk 0.9.3 on a VM 2) trigger auth rotation from our auth service (short-lived tokens) 3) observe a 401 in the server logs then generator stops yielding.

snippet of client log:
```
INFO streaming: connected
data: {"delta":"Hello wor"}
data: {"delta":"ld"}
keep-alive
WARN auth: refresh requested, swapping token
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
# after this, no more `data:` lines show up even though server kept sending valid SSE frames
```

maya: note: server shows continued SSE frames (verified with tcpdump), but python generator yields None / blocks on next iteration. appears like partial token boundary or parser state after auth switch.

rachel: interesting — could be the SSE parser state machine getting stuck when a 401/reauth race interrupts the keep-alive boundary. do we have the raw bytes around the auth swap? any `event:` lines present?

maya: raw bytes around event boundary (truncated):
```
...
data: {"delta":"more"}


HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Connection: close

<reconnect sequence>
data: {"delta":"after-reauth"}
```

maya: they use header token rotation (X-Auth: <short-lived>), not cookies. SDK attaches token per-request but our reconnect path isn't doing a fresh SSE handshake in this case, it tries to continue the generator.

samir: what if SDK tries to reuse the existing response object after a 401? that could leave the SSE parser mid-frame and block. can you confirm python sdk version? 0.9.3 earlier — are there any newer releases?

maya: yes 0.9.3. customer is on 3rd-party infra, can't upgrade easily. asked them to try a quick workaround: pre-emptively close stream and re-open on 401.

rachel: short-term workaround: detect 401 on control path and force full reconnect (new SSE handshake). I'll open an internal issue to add a defensive check so parser cleans state on connection interruption. @eng-bot can you create an issue in the runtime tracker and tag eng-runtime?

eng-bot: created ISSUE-4721: "sse-parser: handle auth-rotation + mid-frame 401 -> ensure reconnect resets parser state" assigned to @rachel, priority P2.

samir: can you also capture request-id from server logs and full timeline? we need to know whether server sent a Connection: close or kept the transport. if server closed it and client didn't observe EOF, that explains the hang.

maya: provided request-ids and timestamps to #support ticket: request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d, logs attached. customer says tcpdump shows server kept sending bytes for ~10s post-401 but client read returned 0 bytes. suspicious.

rachel: okay, I'll pair with eng-runtime tomorrow to reproduce locally by rotating token mid-stream. plan: add a unit test that injects a 401 mid-chunk and assert generator yields reconnect events (or raises gracefully).

samir: possible mitigation for customers: set `streaming_keepalive_interval` lower and enable `retry_on_transport_error` so SDK will detect socket staleness faster. also consider turning on our diagnostic `sse_raw_dump` to collect exact wire frames.

maya: shared quick commands for capture:
```bash
# tcpdump for a single flow
sudo tcpdump -s 0 -w capture.pcap host <server-ip> and port 443
# python repro runner
python repro_stream_hang.py --token-ttl 5s --rotate-after 12s
```

support-bot: escalation routed to eng-runtime & sdk team; ETA initial triage 24h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

rachel: thanks @maya. i'll follow up here with the issue link and a small repro harness. if we can get a minimal script that reproduces on our infra, we can push a patch to make the parser tolerant of mid-stream auth handoffs.

maya: will relay to customer and collect the raw capture. closing loop once we have repro. :+1:
